title: Geriatric Patients, Hemodynamics, Delirium, and Cerebral Inflammation in Orthopedic Surgery
summary: Many patients suffer from an altered state of conciesness and memory after surgery - a postoperative delirium. Even though this state is reversible, it leads to a prolonged convalescence and an increased mortality. However, the underlying causes are not completely known. This study focuses on the reduction of postoperative delirium by an individually blood pressure control during the surgery. Blood pressure is based on the individual mean night-time arterial pressure and is set between the mean night-time mean arterial pressure and the maximum night-time mean arterial pressure during anesthesia. Included are patients older than 70 years undergoing a total hip arthroplasty or a total knee arthroplasty.
conditions: Delirium, not induced by alcohol and other psychoactive substances

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- elective total hip arthroplasty (THA) or total knee arthroplasty (TKA)
- general anesthesia with or without peripheral nerve block
Exclusion criteria:
- known psychiatric disorders (psychosis, major depression) or other cognitive impairment
- language barrier or impaired hearing
- no legal competence
